source.title: Shorter, but Still Trustworthy? An Empirical Study of Chain-of-Thought Compression
source.authors: Li Zeng; Xiao-Fan Chen; Yan-Bo Wang; Xiu-Ying Chen

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates safety outcomes after several CoT-compression methods, extending assessment of alignment-related safety changes to a compression setting. It does not test the specific fine-tuning, token-position, bypass, parameter-localization, or safety-deepening interventions in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures HarmBench refusal accuracy and, for Qwen3-8B, AgentHarm harmful-task completion after compression. It does not fine-tune on harmful examples or test ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning, per-token KL, compliant-token prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-specific parameter edits, or safety-deepening. Prior-work results cited in the text are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Several compressed models are fine-tuned or RL-trained on benign data (L1 length-control RL, Thinkless, VeriThinker, O1-Pruner, and the authors' LoRA DPO on UltraFeedback/SHP), then compared with matched baselines on HarmBench refusal and AgentHarm harmful completion. That is a new-setting test of V2: benign training on safety-trained reasoning models. Prompting (BeConcise), TokenSkip and weight merging are not fine-tuning, so they bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that CoT compression often causes trustworthiness regressions, including up to 10 points of safety, with method- and base-dependent profiles. Their DPO variant shows compression with limited loss, but does not isolate DPO from the data.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates CoT compression methods and their safety outcomes; it does not reproduce the original harmful- or benign-example fine-tuning intervention or the first-token KL and compliant-prefill tests. It cites prior benign-fine-tuning work as context.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety outcomes vary by compression method and base model. On Qwen3-8B, L1 lowers HarmBench refusal accuracy while BeConcise, TokenSkip and DPO have different profiles; AgentHarm changes in a different direction for some methods. The paper also reports variation among merging strategies on DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompt-based (BeConcise), token-removal (TokenSkip) and weight-merging compression change HarmBench/AgentHarm safety in mixed directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-training CoT-compression interventions can shift harmful-prompt refusal up or down depending on method and base.

record.problems: The primary HarmBench evaluation relies on Llama Guard 3; the paper audits 513 sampled judgments and reports agreement, but acknowledges that item-level validation is limited to that subset. AgentHarm is reported only for models with sufficient agentic capability. The reported primary table values do not include per-model confidence intervals or error bars.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported HarmBench or AgentHarm outcomes was left out. Other trustworthiness dimensions and reasoning-accuracy results were excluded because they do not measure the behaviors named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: No dose-response over number of examples, no plain benign SFT on instruction data, and no deliberately selected benign data aimed at breaking safety. Bases often have low initial refusal (18–31%).
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked V2 not tested, but several compression methods are benign fine-tuning or RL on safety-trained models, so those rows are relinked to V2. Caveats: three DeepSeek distill bases start with very low refusal (18–31%), which limits how much erosion can show. The DPO data was filtered for shorter, higher-quality chosen responses but contains no safety data. All results use greedy decoding, a Llama Guard 3 judge and a single run with no CIs. Baseline control rows stay at none.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or harmful-example count is tested.

DPO uses preference pairs filtered for shorter, higher-quality chosen responses as part of a compression method; the paper does not test ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction fine-tuning as the claimed intervention.
No per-token KL divergence or aligned-versus-base response-position comparison.
No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass test.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
The proposed explanations are conjectures; the study does not test what produces first-token shallowness.
The DPO variant compresses reasoning; it does not train safety to be deeper across response positions or test whether such deepening holds up.
